description: Holds gives the values of every step of an explanation, in the explanation's order
code:
price = 10
qty = 3
shipping = 5
subtotal = price * qty
total = subtotal + shipping
total |> why |> holds

description: Holds after stated gives the values of the facts that a conclusion rests on
code:
seed = 2
middle = seed + 3
result = middle * 2
result |> why |> stated |> holds

description: Holds after derived gives the values of the conclusions on the way to a value
code:
seed = 2
middle = seed + 3
result = middle * 2
result |> why |> derived |> holds

description: Holds after affects gives the values that a change of one fact reaches
code:
rate = 0.5
price = 10
subtotal = price * 3
tax = subtotal * rate
total = subtotal + tax
price |> affects |> holds

description: Holds of the model gives the value of every node, without the declarations that hold a stage
code:
a = 1
b = a + 1
values = b |> why |> holds
model |> holds

description: Holds gives strings and booleans as the steps hold them
code:
name = "Ada"
title = "Dr"
label = title + " " + name
long = label.length > 5
long |> why |> holds

description: A reference alone gives its own value as a list of one
code:
price = 10
qty = 3
total = price * qty
[total |> holds, price |> holds]

description: A prefix stage and depth before holds give the values within one step
code:
price = 10
qty = 3
shipping = 5
subtotal = price * qty
total = subtotal + shipping
why total |> depth(1) |> holds

description: Holds after union gives the values behind either of two results, each node once
code:
price = 10
quantity = 3
rate = 0.5
subtotal = price * quantity
tax = subtotal * rate
shipping = quantity * 2
tax |> why |> union(shipping |> why) |> holds

description: Holds after intersect gives the values of the causes that two results share
code:
price = 10
quantity = 3
rate = 0.5
subtotal = price * quantity
tax = subtotal * rate
shipping = quantity * 2
tax |> why |> intersect(shipping |> why) |> holds

description: A standing declaration of held values follows a rewiring and a change of value
code:
a = 1
b = a + 2
c = b * 2
values = c |> why |> holds
x = 5
b = x + 1
x = 7
values

description: A class-level rule holds the values behind each instance's own total
code:
class Order(price, qty):
    this.price = price
    this.qty = qty
$Order.total = $Order.price * $Order.qty
$Order.basis = $Order.total |> why |> holds
first = Order(10, 2)
second = Order(4, 5)
first.qty = 3
[first.basis, second.basis]
